title: Bayesian posterior over Mirror coordinates
hypothesis: A Gaussian posterior over a one-dimensional Mirror coordinate can represent a three-mode logistic posterior with matched predictive calibration using at least 10% fewer bytes than a matched rank-1 multiplicative BNN and independent three-model mixture.
physical_object: one 16-dimensional logistic classifier mean and a sparse one-coordinate functional direction
mirror_coordinate: Gaussian scalar m with five-node Gauss-Hermite predictive integration
logical_multiplicity: continuous uncertainty over nearby logistic functions, approximated deterministically for prediction

development.selection_metric: predictive NLL, Brier, ECE, calibration MSE, shifted NLL, actual bytes, quadrature component compute

storage.authority: actual deterministic ZIP/NPY FP32 inference payload after reload
paid_objects: posterior location and scale or discrete factors

success_gate: Both development seeds: NLL within 0.01 of exact teacher, calibration MSE <=1e-4, ECE <=0.03, Mirror >=10% smaller than rank-1 BNN and independent three-model archive, compute <=1.5x BNN; direct scalar control >=10% larger or measurably worse calibrated for Mirror-specific claim.
failure_gate: Either dev seed misses quality gates, byte savings <10%, rank-1 BNN within 10% bytes at equal quality, direct scalar control within 10%, or compute >1.5x; fresh sealed.
boundaries: oracle synthetic posterior, no posterior fitting
deterministic quadrature approximates continuous Gaussian predictions and is charged for five components
